title: ArtCraft (storytold): 17 Rust Native Creative and Office Apps
excerpt: Explore storytold ArtCraft and its 17 open-source Crafting Apps built in native Rust, cross-platform installers, Flatpak OCI packages, and Cargo build steps.
body:
Replacing commercial creative and office software often forces an awkward compromise: Electron wrappers eat memory on basic tasks, while older open-source tools require relearning years of muscle memory. The GitHub organization `storytold` takes another path with ArtCraft (`getartcraft.com`), rebuilding creative and productivity suites natively in Rust.

![Official ArtCraft branding alongside icons of the Crafting Apps suite](/news/assets/artcraft-open-source-tools-72b72d44.webp)

Within `storytold`, ArtCraft splits cleanly into two complementary tracks: ArtCraft Studio for AI image and video creation, and Crafting Apps, an umbrella of 17 standalone native desktop applications managed by ArtCraft Launcher.

## Two Lines: ArtCraft Studio and 17 Crafting Apps

ArtCraft Studio (`storytold/artcraft`) gives artists a 2D composition workspace and 3D canvas for staging scenes before rendering with AI image or video models. Its official downloads page currently lists desktop release `0.41.1` alongside a browser edition at `app.getartcraft.com`.

Separate from the AI studio, Crafting Apps spans 17 native applications written from scratch in pure Rust using the `egui` toolkit and `wgpu` GPU abstraction. All 17 run offline locally with no Electron runtime, release their source code under dual permissive MIT or Apache-2.0 terms, and represent every edit as a structured command runnable from the GUI, CLI, JSON control channel, or MCP server. Sixteen of the tools also target WebAssembly for browser execution, with FilmCraft staying focused on desktop editing.

The 17 official Crafting Apps divide naturally across three creative workflows:

- Graphics, photo, and document publishing cover PhotoCraft (raster editing and `.psd` support), VectorCraft (vector illustration), LightCraft (photo library and non-destructive RAW processor), DesignCraft (page layout and publishing), FigCraft (interface design and prototyping), and PdfCraft (PDF reading, organization, and editing).
- Video, animation, audio, and 3D work bring FilmCraft (non-linear video editor), EffectCraft (motion graphics and compositing), AniCraft (2D vector animation), SoundCraft (Digital Audio Workstation), TextureCraft (3D texture painting), and MaterialCraft (node-based procedural material authoring).
- Office, engineering, and utility software span WordCraft (a `.docx` word processor with ribbon, styles, and track changes), GridCraft (spreadsheets and data analysis), DeckCraft (slide decks), CADCraft (2D/3D CAD), and Craft Anything for inspecting how software works and assembling custom apps.

Beyond the core 17, the ArtCraft Launcher catalog also indexes two community-maintained apps: SolidCraft (parametric 3D CAD by Tangency Labs) and MailCraft (email, calendar, and contacts by UCS Labs).

## Cross-Platform Installers Across Windows, macOS, and Linux

The team recommends installing through ArtCraft Launcher (`storytold/craft-launcher`). From one desktop window or system tray menu, the launcher detects your operating system and CPU architecture, downloads official GitHub releases per app, checks binaries against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, handles updates, and manages typefaces through Craft Font Manager. Individual standalone installers are equally available at `getartcraft.com/apps`.

Platform packaging covers Windows, macOS, Linux, and BSD without community hacks. Windows 10 and 11 offer `.msi` installers for `x64`, `arm64`, and `x86` (supporting per-user `x64` installs without administrator rights) alongside portable `.zip` bundles. macOS 11 or newer receives a signed, notarized universal `.dmg` for both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Linux builds ship as `.AppImage`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.flatpak`, and `.tar.gz` for `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and `riscv64`, backed by signed repositories at `getartcraft.com/linux` for Flatpak OCI, APT, DNF, Zypper, and Pacman, plus tarballs for FreeBSD 14.

## Installing via Flatpak OCI or Building From Source

Linux users can add the official Flatpak OCI repository without root access, while Rust developers with `1.90+` installed can compile the launcher directly from GitHub:

```bash
# Option 1: Register official Flatpak OCI remote and install launcher + PdfCraft
flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists artcraft-oci https://getartcraft.com/artcraft-oci.flatpakrepo
flatpak install --user artcraft-oci ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher ai.storyteller.pdfcraft

# Option 2: Build ArtCraft Launcher from source (Linux requires X11/Wayland/Mesa dev headers)
git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher.git
cd craft-launcher
cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher
```

The first two `flatpak` commands register the `artcraft-oci` remote at user scope and pull signed releases directly. The Cargo workflow clones `craft-launcher` and compiles the release binary natively for your host architecture.

## Development Status and Brand Boundaries

Most applications in Crafting Apps and ArtCraft Launcher are still actively maturing in *in development* or *early alpha* stages, including PhotoCraft, PdfCraft, AniCraft, FigCraft, and Craft Anything. While the application codebases allow modification and redistribution under MIT or Apache-2.0 licenses, `storytold` keeps ArtCraft trademark rights separate so forks cannot reuse the official name or logos without permission.
